result.summary: This PR patches contrib/linearize/linearize-data.py to avoid destructively truncating pre-existing output files when the script is re-run, and to truncate trailing block data left over after a chain reorg. It changes the file open mode from 'wb' (which always truncates) to an exclusive-create-or-reopen pattern, and adds explicit ftruncate calls at file rotation points.
result.problem: Users who run linearize-data repeatedly against a live node (e.g. to keep a rolling bootstrap dataset) currently have their output files fully truncated and rewritten from scratch on every run, and reorgs can leave stale trailing data in output files. This is disruptive for anyone consuming the files while they are being regenerated.

result.card: This PR (contrib: Support re-writing linearize-data dumps) fixes contrib/linearize/linearize-data.py so re-running the script against a live node no longer truncates existing output files to zero bytes, and trims stray trailing block data left after a chain reorg. The problem affects operators who repeatedly regenerate linearize dumps for ongoing use, as demonstrated by a reproduction script from another user showing continuous file truncation without the fix. It is a tiny 6-line diff with one reviewer (sedited) ultimately ACKing it as harmless and useful, though the author has been silent for roughly six months despite a lingering request to make the PR description explicitly describe the re-write behavior rather than framing it purely as a bug fix. No dependencies or blocking technical objections exist, and the priority is capped because linearize-data is a low-traffic contrib tool.
